purpose: Cross the source-capacity gate left by v7.6.1. Exhaust every smooth Hamiltonian C16 representation with four complementary C4 components, designate components 0 and 1 as terminals and 2 and 3 as hidden components, keep every Hamiltonian edge incident with a hidden component, and open the interface only by deleting k Hamiltonian edges directly between terminals 0 and 1. Determine exactly when the projected terminal orbit relation becomes a three-state bijection while both terminals retain reusable Hamiltonian capacity.

model.smooth_word: A rooted cyclic word of length 16 over {0,1,2,3}, each symbol occurring exactly four times, first symbol fixed to 0, and no equal cyclic neighbours. The j-th occurrence of component i is port j of its complementary C4. Hence each complementary C4 is non-selfcrossing relative to the Hamiltonian order by construction.
model.full_H_edges: Adjacent symbols in the cyclic word are the sixteen Hamiltonian edges. Each C4 port has exactly two Hamiltonian incidences in the full source graph.
model.opening_rule: Delete only k edges whose component pair is {0,1}. Therefore hidden components 2 and 3 remain fully H-saturated, while each deleted edge creates one free Hamiltonian half-edge on terminal 0 and one on terminal 1.
model.terminal_relation: For each terminal orbit pair (tau0,tau1) in {0,1,2}^2, existentially quantify all S3 gauges and both hidden orbit types. Global colour symmetry fixes terminal-0 gauge to identity. The resulting subset R of {0,1,2}^2 is exact.
model.bijection_test: R is an orbit wire exactly when it is the graph of a permutation pi in S3, i.e. R={(a,pi(a)):a in {0,1,2}}. This transmits only the C4 orbit type; it does not assert unique or preserved S3 gauge transport.

exhaustive_capacity_threshold.theorem: Within this complete four-C4 hidden-saturated opening class, k=3 is the unique cut count that realizes an exact three-state orbit bijection. In particular the previous >=2-free-half-edge capacity gate is genuinely crossed, but only after three terminal-terminal Hamiltonian edges are opened.

explicit_positive_control.hidden_saturation: Every Hamiltonian edge incident with component 2 or 3 from the parent C16 is retained, so every hidden port still has Hamiltonian degree two.
explicit_positive_control.interpretation: The partial source gadget gives an exact twisted orbit wire with three free Hamiltonian half-edges on each terminal. It is stronger than the asymmetric v7.6.1 three-C4 partial control, whose second terminal had only one free half-edge.

proof_and_replay: Enumerate all 455058 rooted smooth words exactly by multiplicity and cyclic-adjacency constraints.

For each word form the six port-labelled intercomponent Hamiltonian bundles. For each k=2,...,7 enumerate every k-subset of the 0--1 bundle and delete exactly those edges; words with fewer than k terminal-terminal edges contribute no opening.

Evaluate each projected terminal relation exactly in the finite orbit-plus-gauge model. For one terminal gauge fixed to identity there are only three orbit choices at that terminal and eighteen local orbit-plus-gauge states at each other component; pair-bundle compatibility is exact and no probabilistic step is used.

Classify each resulting 3x3 Boolean relation by cardinality and compare it with all six permutation graphs. The checker reproduces every count frozen above and independently verifies the displayed positive control.

positive: The true smooth/non-selfcrossing source class supports a reusable-capacity exact three-state orbit transport atom; cyclic holonomy is not merely a closed obstruction.
Three opened terminal-terminal Hamiltonian edges are sufficient to leave three free source half-edges on each terminal while hidden components remain saturated.
The orbit transport is a finite permutation, suggesting a gain/backbone representation for networks of such atoms rather than generic 3^r orbit enumeration.
firewall: This is an orbit-type wire only. S3 gauges are existential and are not proved to propagate as a unique gain through the gadget.
A partial gadget is not yet a completed hard-source instance. Adding external Hamiltonian edges can shrink the terminal relation; relation-preserving source completion is not automatic.
No claim is made that arbitrary logical wire networks can be embedded into one Hamiltonian cycle while preserving smooth C4 order.
This does not construct a polynomial 3-COLOR or SAT algorithm and does not imply P=NP.
negative: Opening exactly two terminal-terminal edges is insufficient for any exact orbit bijection in the complete four-C4 class despite meeting the old >=2 total free-half-edge threshold.
More opening is not monotonically better: k=4,...,7 realize no exact orbit bijection in this class.

next_target.directive: Treat the v7.7 three-cut twisted orbit wire as a partial factor, not a finished reduction gadget. Determine whether its six free half-edges can be connected through additional smooth C4 source pieces so that (i) the global H-edges form one Hamiltonian cycle, (ii) every added and retained complementary C4 remains non-selfcrossing, (iii) the exact projected relation on the two named terminals remains the same bijection, and (iv) enough controlled interface remains for composition. In parallel compute whether the satisfying gauge relation conditioned on each orbit pair is a single S3 gain coset or a larger set. If unique/coset gain transport holds, compile networks to a polynomial group-gain backbone; if not, freeze the smallest explicit gauge-branching barrier.
